column11: Radiotrophic melanized yeast. A yeast cell is near-isotropic, so the blob attractor is not obviously wrong for it — but V_target is shared with six other species, so the parcel reading still holds.
Coccus, and in reality a tetrad-forming one. Cell shape is near-isotropic; tetrad structure is not represented.

FILAMENTOUS FUNGUS. A hypha needs elongation and connectivity terms that compute_delta_H does not have, so it cannot be represented as anything but a blob. Whether a parcel here means a compartment, a conidium or a length of mycelium is UNRESOLVED and matters for any dose-per-organism claim.
MOTILE ROD. No elongation term exists, so the rod relaxes to a blob; the per-species motility vector D_s is declared in CPMParams but never read by the acceptance test either.
FILAMENTOUS FUNGUS, melanized. Same limitation as C. sphaerospermum; conidia and hyphae are not distinguished.
Metal-reducing rod. Load-bearing for the material branch: X_red is currently the site fraction of this species, which is neither a mass fraction nor an active-reducer fraction.

Thorium-tolerant EPS producer. EPS is not a separate phase in the model; a parcel bundles cells and their extracellular material together, which is what makes the hydrated-bulk material reading the compatible one.
